Sure, here are two hints for the given step:

**Hint 1:** Consider what it means to one-hot encode a sequence. Each unique sequence of letters (in this case, DNA letters) will have its own dimension in the encoding. For a whole DNA string, think about how many possible sequences there are.

**Hint 2:** Remember that each position in the DNA string can be one of four letters: T, G, C, or A. To find the total number of dimensions for one-hot encoding the entire string, consider the number of possible combinations of these letters across all positions in the string.
